title: HermesAgent-20 — recommended thinking, two retained first-attempt passes
score_definition: Arithmetic average of the two official pass scores. Unrounded task-score mean is a separate measure.
wall_definition: case_wall_seconds_mean averages the two sums of saved task durations; suite_elapsed_seconds_mean averages first task dispatch to last verifier completion, retaining between-task gaps. Neither includes model loading or restoration.
replay_definition: Mean mode is a synchronized reconstruction using each task’s two-run mean measured duration; it excludes between-task gaps. Pass 1/2 retain actual case UTC timestamps and elapsed offsets. Participants were run sequentially, not simultaneously. Tool event ordering is verified, but no reliable subcall timing is claimed.
limitations: Carlos HC-Q8 publisher-current Hermes ran on Ciru; the original six and Orca ran on Sozo. Do not interpret its wall-time position as a controlled same-host performance ranking.
Halogen retained its 45,056-token native output ceiling because a full-context output allocation exceeded Sozo memory; output allowance was not identical across stacks.
Carlos pass 2 HA-07 reached the 1,800-second case boundary and scored zero. It has no final agent-result record or complete primary-tool count.
Official scores and verifier pass/partial/fail are distinct: for example, HA-17 may receive 70/100 while retaining a fail verdict. Mean task status is mixed when the two verdicts differ.
Hermes tool-internal summarizers retain task-specific sampling/output budgets. One v5 pass-1 delegated request inherited matching settings from server defaults; later stages made them explicit.
The replay is a visualization of recorded case durations, not a recording of concurrent agent execution or individually timed tool calls.
Orca is part of the approved Hermes/storage extension only; no absent panels are inferred.
